column1: # EXP-R2-212 attainability probe: two-site Crosscoders at d_hidden 16,384, both modes, two seeds each.
# Columns, tab-separated: slot <TAB> key <TAB> gpu <TAB> stage <TAB> label <TAB> env <TAB> args
# DISPATCH ONLY AFTER the lambda=0 text replicates are read. If they clear the adequacy bar at 8,192 the text cells
# here are unnecessary and this manifest must be cut before use; the projection says they will not, but "unlikely" is
# ONE CELL PER CARD, four cards, one wave. Each cell is ~81,508 MiB live of 143,771 by the measured decomposition
# (analytic 58,479 x the observed 1.394 allocator overhead) -- 57% of the card, 43% headroom.
# THE ENV COLUMN CARRIES THE ALLOCATOR SETTING, and this is the first use of that column. PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF is
# an allocator setting and NOT a recipe parameter -- it changes how device memory is reserved and reused, not what is
# computed -- so live-latent counts stay comparable with cells trained without it. Declared as a deviation. Applied
# from the START rather than after a loss, because the precedent cell survived its squeeze only by releasing 31 GB of
# cache and a cell under memory pressure has almost none to release. EXP-R2-193's text cells had to be HAND-LAUNCHED for this, since
# run_external_baseline_h200.sh sources h200_env.sh from the frozen snapshot and forwards no caller environment; the
# queue's env column removes that need, so these cells keep a dispatch record instead of being hand-launched.
# IF A CELL OOMs IT IS A FAILURE AND THE ROUND STOPS. Width, sites and batch are the recipe; a cell rescued by
# reducing any of them is incomparable with everything it would be read against, which is worse than a failed cell.
# The allocator path above is the only permitted recovery and it is already applied.
# VOID CONDITIONS unchanged: protein 36,978 steps / 34,001,183 scored tokens, screen 961 of 1,024 at 1.0000 over
